narrator: Mina Murray (journal) and Dr. John Seward (phonograph diary)
dates: Mina: 24 July - 6 August; Seward: 5 June - 20 July
summary: Mina arrives at Whitby on 24 July, is met by Lucy, and describes the town, the Esk valley, the ruined abbey, the steep churchyard on the cliff and the harbour with its two lighthouses and bell-buoy. She befriends Mr. Swales, an ancient sceptical sailor who mocks tombstones and legends, notably the suicide's grave of George Canon on which Lucy's favourite seat rests. Interleaved, Seward's diary tracks Renfield's escalating chain of pets (flies, spiders, sparrows, a requested kitten), culminating in Renfield eating his birds raw; Seward diagnoses a zoophagous (life-eating) maniac. Mina worries as Jonathan sends only a one-line letter from Castle Dracula and then goes silent, while Lucy resumes sleepwalking and Mina locks the bedroom door each night. On 6 August a grey, ominous storm builds; Swales, gentle and shaken, speaks of death in the wind, and a coastguard watches a strange Russian ship that is steered erratically.

scenes.title: Arrival at Whitby and the view
scenes.location: The Crescent, Whitby; Esk valley; East Cliff
scenes.summary: Lucy meets Mina at the station; they drive to rooms at the Crescent. Mina describes the viaduct, red-roofed old town, Whitby Abbey ruin and the clifftop churchyard.
scenes.key_quote: Right over the town is the ruin of Whitby Abbey, which was sacked by the Danes.

scenes.title: The harbour and the bell-buoy
scenes.location: Whitby harbour seen from the churchyard
scenes.summary: Mina describes the two piers with lighthouses, the tidal harbour, the reef with a bell buoy and the legend that bells are heard when a ship is lost.
scenes.key_quote: At the end of it is a buoy with a bell, which swings in bad weather, and sends in a mournful sound on the wind.

scenes.title: First meeting with the old man
scenes.summary: Nearly-hundred-year-old ex-whaler dismisses the White Lady and sea bells as 'fool-talk' and hobbles home for tea down the hundreds of curved steps.
scenes.key_quote: I wouldn't fash masel' about them, miss. Them things be all wore out.

scenes.title: Swales on tombstones and Geordie's grave
scenes.summary: Swales rants that half the tombstones cover empty graves because men were lost at sea, and exposes the slab where Lucy sits as the grave of George Canon, a suicide who shot himself with a crow-scaring musket and fell from Kettleness rocks.
scenes.key_quote: Won't it make Gabriel keckle when Geordie comes pantin' up the grees with the tombstean balanced on his hump.

scenes.title: Night view of Whitby
scenes.summary: Mina, sad with no letter from Jonathan, watches the lights, hears sheep, a donkey, a harsh waltz and a Salvation Army meeting.
scenes.key_quote: The clock has just struck nine. I see the lights scattered all over the town.

scenes.title: Renfield's flies and spiders
scenes.summary: Renfield collects flies, then spiders to eat the flies, and eats a blow-fly, saying it is life. He keeps a notebook of columns of figures and tames a sparrow.
scenes.key_quote: it was very good and very wholesome; that it was life, strong life, and gave life to him.

scenes.title: The kitten request and eaten birds
scenes.summary: Renfield begs for a kitten, then a cat, and when refused sits gnawing his fingers. Next morning the sparrows are gone, with feathers and a drop of blood on his pillow; he vomits feathers. Seward drugs him with an opiate, takes his notebook and names him zoophagous.
scenes.key_quote: He has eaten his birds, and that he just took and ate them raw!

scenes.title: Anxiety, sleepwalking and the locked door
scenes.location: Mina and Lucy's shared room at the Crescent
scenes.summary: Jonathan's only word is a line from Castle Dracula saying he is starting home, via Mr. Hawkins. Lucy sleepwalks again; Mina locks the door, and Lucy searches the room for the key while asleep.
scenes.key_quote: She tries the door, and finding it locked, goes about the room searching for the key.

scenes.title: Grey storm day, Swales's change, the strange ship
scenes.summary: Mina describes the grey sea under massing clouds. Swales confesses his mocking was to cheer himself and feels death in the wind; the coastguard points out an erratically steered Russian ship.
scenes.key_quote: She doesn't know her mind a bit; she seems to see the storm coming, but can't decide whether to run up north in the open, or to put in here.

locations.name: The Crescent, Whitby
locations.description: Terrace of rooms where the Westenras and Mina lodge.
locations.quote: we drove up to the house at the Crescent in which they have rooms

locations.name: Whitby town and Esk valley
locations.description: Deep green steep valley with the small River Esk, a great viaduct on high piers, and old red-roofed houses piled up like Nuremberg.
locations.quote: The houses of the old town are all red-roofed, and seem piled up one over the other anyhow

locations.name: Whitby Abbey ruin
locations.description: Immense noble ruin above the town, sacked by the Danes, with a legend of a white lady at a window.
locations.quote: there is a legend that a white lady is seen in one of the windows

locations.name: St. Mary's churchyard (East Cliff)
locations.description: Large graveyard of tombstones on a steep cliff above the harbour; erosion has collapsed graves, with stonework hanging over the sandy path far below. Walks with seats run through it.
features: slab-stone seat over the Canon grave near cliff edge
collapsed bank with exposed grave stonework
old house next to the abbey
locations.atmosphere: peaceful by day, ominous in grey weather
locations.quote: part of the stonework of the graves stretches out over the sandy pathway far below

locations.name: The 199 steps (church stairs)
locations.description: Hundreds of steps winding in a delicate gentle curve from town to church, so shallow a horse could walk them (number not stated).
locations.quote: there are hundreds of them—I do not know how many—and they wind up in a delicate curve

locations.name: Whitby harbour
locations.description: Long granite wall with a curved end and lighthouse on the far side, a heavy sea-wall outside; a crooked elbow pier with lighthouse on the near side; narrow opening between the piers, tidal sand flats at low water.
features: reef with bell buoy half a mile out
locations.quote: Between the two piers there is a narrow opening into the harbour, which then suddenly widens.

locations.name: Renfield's cell
locations.description: Asylum room with a window where he puts sugar to attract flies, a pillow, boxes of spiders.
locations.quote: He was spreading out his sugar, which he had saved, in the window

characters.name: Mr. Swales
characters.role: Ancient local sailor, 'Sir Oracle' of the cliff-top bench
characters.appearance: face gnarled and twisted like tree bark, nearly a hundred, hobbles with a stick
characters.personality: sceptical, dictatorial, bullying in debate, secretly afraid of death, gentle at last
notable_lines: It be all fool-talk, lock, stock, and barrel.
There's something in that wind... that sounds, and looks, and tastes, and smells like death.

characters.name: Lucy Westenra
characters.appearance: sweet and lovely, beautiful colour, rose-pink cheeks, a trifle stouter, lost anaemic look
notable_lines: It is my favourite seat, and I cannot leave it.

characters.name: R. M. Renfield
characters.personality: selfish, secretive, purposeful, cruelly fond of animals; fawns like a dog
notable_lines: A kitten, a nice little, sleek playful kitten, that I can play with, and teach, and feed—and feed—and feed!

characters.name: Dr. John Seward
notable_lines: I shall have to invent a new classification for him, and call him a zoöphagous (life-eating) maniac.

characters.name: Coastguard
notable_lines: We'll hear more of her before this time to-morrow.

characters.name: Mr. Hawkins
characters.role: Jonathan's employer who forwards the letter

characters.name: Hon. Arthur Holmwood
characters.role: Lucy's fiance, son of Lord Godalming

objects.name: George Canon's slab
objects.description: A flat thruff-stean laid as a bench-slab near the cliff edge, engraved with a pious epitaph over a suicide's grave.
objects.function_in_story: Lucy's favourite seat; where she is later drawn at night.
objects.quote: Sacred to the memory of George Canon, who died, in the hope of a glorious resurrection, on July, 29, 1873

objects.name: Edward Spencelagh gravestone
objects.description: Stone for a master mariner murdered by pirates off Andres, 1854, age 30.
objects.function_in_story: Swales's example of a lie, empty grave.
objects.quote: Edward Spencelagh, master mariner, murdered by pirates off the coast of Andres, April, 1854

objects.name: Bell buoy
objects.description: Buoy with a bell at end of reef, swings in bad weather.
objects.function_in_story: Sea legend of bells when a ship is lost.
objects.location_or_owner: end of the reef south of the south lighthouse
objects.quote: At the end of it is a buoy with a bell

objects.name: Old musket
objects.description: Old musket kept for scaring crows, used by Geordie to shoot himself.
objects.quote: an old musket that they had for scarin' the crows

objects.name: Spy-glass
objects.quote: the coastguard came along, with his spy-glass under his arm

objects.name: Renfield's note-book
objects.description: Pocket-book full of columns of single numbers summed in batches and totals summed again, like an auditor's account.
objects.function_in_story: Seward takes it to read; Renfield's book-keeping of lives.
objects.quote: Whole pages of it are filled with masses of figures

objects.name: Sugar
objects.description: Saved sugar spread on the window sill to attract flies.
objects.quote: spreading out his sugar, which he had saved, in the window

objects.name: Spider box
objects.description: Box holding several very big spiders.
objects.quote: several very big fellows in a box

objects.name: Opiate
objects.description: A strong dose strong enough to make even Renfield sleep.
objects.function_in_story: Seward sedates him to search his pocket-book.
objects.quote: I gave Renfield a strong opiate to-night, enough to make even him sleep

objects.name: Letter from Castle Dracula
objects.description: One line dated Castle Dracula saying he is starting home; handwriting is Jonathan's but reads unlike him.
objects.quote: It is only a line dated from Castle Dracula, and says that he is just starting for home.

objects.name: Bedroom door key
objects.description: Key Mina uses to lock their room against Lucy's sleepwalking; Lucy searches for it asleep.
objects.quote: I am to lock the door of our room every night

creatures.name: The White Lady of the abbey
creatures.description: Legendary figure seen in an abbey window.
creatures.behaviour: Seen at a window (legend only; Swales dismisses it).
creatures.quote: there is a legend that a white lady is seen in one of the windows

creatures.name: Bell-ghosts at sea
creatures.description: Legend that bells are heard when a ship is lost.
creatures.quote: They have a legend here that when a ship is lost bells are heard out at sea.

creatures.name: Folk spirits (bans, wafts, boh-ghosts, barguests, bogles)
creatures.description: Local ghost types listed by Swales.
creatures.behaviour: Said to scare children and dizzy women.
creatures.quote: These bans an' wafts an' boh-ghosts an' barguests an' bogles

creatures.name: Renfield's swarm (flies, spiders, sparrows)
creatures.description: Chain of animals harvested by Renfield.
creatures.behaviour: Flies eaten by spiders, spiders by sparrows.
creatures.quote: He gave many flies to one spider and many spiders to one bird

vampire_lore.rule: Renfield believes eating living things grants life
vampire_lore.detail: He eats a blow-fly and claims it is life, strong life; accumulates lives cumulatively.
vampire_lore.quote: it was life, strong life, and gave life to him

vampire_lore.rule: Lucy sleepwalks and seeks the key; the suicide's grave is her seat
vampire_lore.detail: Foreshadows nightly summoning; sleepwalking intensifies once the storm and ship approach.
vampire_lore.quote: even in her sleep she seems to be watching me

vampire_lore.rule: A suicide's grave on cliff edge
vampire_lore.detail: Folk belief of a bad burial; later site of Dracula's attacks (inferred).
vampire_lore.quote: I must go on sitting over the grave of a suicide.

puzzles.name: Renfield's chain of lives
puzzles.setup: Renfield's pets keep vanishing and growing in size.
puzzles.obstacle: Seward must decode the pattern behind the madness.
puzzles.book_solution: Seward watches the diminishing flies and spiders, finds the sparrows' feathers and blood, sedates Renfield and reads his notebook.
puzzles.game_idea: Deduction board: arrange pet counts over days to reveal the food chain and predict Renfield's next demand; success unlocks the diagnosis and lets the player pre-empt his next move.
puzzles.quote: He gave many flies to one spider and many spiders to one bird, and then wanted a cat to eat the many birds.

puzzles.name: Reading Whitby's tombstones
puzzles.setup: Swales claims half the stones are lies.
puzzles.obstacle: Find which gravestones are true or cenotaphs.
puzzles.book_solution: Swales reads inscriptions and tells stories behind them.
puzzles.game_idea: Investigation mini-game: read inscriptions, compare death places with burial and tell true graves from empty ones (and spot where new vampire graves would appear).
puzzles.quote: there be scores of these lay-beds that be toom as old Dun's 'bacca-box on Friday night.

puzzles.name: Locked room vs sleepwalker
puzzles.obstacle: Keep Lucy inside; she hunts for the key.
puzzles.book_solution: Mina locks the door every night; Lucy searches for the key.
puzzles.game_idea: Stealth/guard mini-game at night: hide the key, listen for movement and keep the sleepwalker safe before she reaches the cliff.
puzzles.quote: She tries the door, and finding it locked, goes about the room searching for the key.

puzzles.name: Reading the weather and the ship
puzzles.setup: A storm approaches and a strange ship wanders.
puzzles.book_solution: Coastguard observes with spy-glass, judges it Russian and badly steered.
puzzles.game_idea: Watch-tower observation puzzle: collect signs (sky colour, ship behaviour, fishermen) to forecast the ship's arrival.
puzzles.quote: She is steered mighty strangely, for she doesn't mind the hand on the wheel.

dialogue_samples.speaker: Mr. Swales
dialogue_samples.line: Lord, make me answer cheerful when my call comes!

dialogue_samples.speaker: Renfield
dialogue_samples.line: May I have three days? I shall clear them away.
dialogue_samples.context: Asked to dispose of his flies.

dialogue_samples.speaker: Renfield
dialogue_samples.line: Oh, yes, I would like a cat! I only asked for a kitten lest you should refuse me a cat.

dialogue_samples.speaker: Coastguard
dialogue_samples.line: We'll hear more of her before this time to-morrow.

dialogue_samples.speaker: Mr. Swales
dialogue_samples.line: Look! look! There's something in that wind and in the hoast beyont that sounds, and looks, and tastes, and smells like death.

asset_candidates.name: East Cliff churchyard
asset_candidates.visual_description: Sloping graveyard of weathered slate tombstones at a cliff edge with eroded bank, exposed grave stonework and benches.

asset_candidates.name: Church steps
asset_candidates.visual_description: Wide shallow stone stair winding in a gentle curve up the hill with handrail.

asset_candidates.name: Whitby harbour with twin lighthouses
asset_candidates.visual_description: Two granite piers with small white lighthouses, narrow mouth, sandbars at low tide and sea-wall.

asset_candidates.name: Bell buoy
asset_candidates.visual_description: Iron buoy with a bell on a frame, swinging in surf on a reef.

asset_candidates.name: George Canon slab
asset_candidates.visual_description: Flat engraved stone slab with a bench resting on it, near the cliff edge.

asset_candidates.name: Renfield's cell
asset_candidates.visual_description: Bare padded-style room with a barred window, sugar smeared on sill, spider box, feathers on pillow.

asset_candidates.name: Russian schooner
asset_candidates.visual_description: Sailing ship staggering in a storm, erratic sails, steered with a lashed wheel.

asset_candidates.name: Storm sea-mist (sea fret)
asset_candidates.visual_description: Grey rolling mist, heaving ground-swell and piled clouds with a sunburst at the horizon.

quest_hooks: Investigate Renfield: collect clues over several nights to classify his madness.
Keep watch on Lucy at night and lock the door before she sleepwalks to the cliff.
Interview Mr. Swales and cronies for graveyard lore; choose to read inscriptions.
Find news of Jonathan: contact Mr. Hawkins and inspect the Castle Dracula letter.
Storm approaching: watch the harbour and identify the Russian ship.
